# /final-experience-report

> [!NOTE]
> Not used in the individual challenge (14:00-17:40). The challenge ends at Stage 3 and judge validation. See [ADR-0003](../../docs/adr/0003-individual-challenge-format.md).

## Objective

Capture the participant's honest reflections on using AI agents throughout the workshop. The agent facilitates the experience reflection but does not write the answers — the participant speaks, and the agent formats.

## When to Invoke

After Stage 4 to preserve actual run status and collect the participant's reflections. Do not consume data
validation time to force all answers into the five-minute reporting interval.

## Preconditions

- The participant completed all four stages (or as many as time allowed)
- The participant is ready to reflect on its experience

## Inputs the Team Must Provide

- Answers to five specific questions (the participant writes them, and the agent formats them)
- The participant name

## What I Will Do

- Present the five experience reflection questions to the participant
- Wait for the participant to answer each question
- Format the answers in a clean document
- Add metadata (participant name, date, completed stages)

## What I Will NOT Do

- Write answers for the participant — every word in the report must come from the participant
- Summarize or editorialize the participant's answers
- Invent answers for questions the participant has not answered; leave them pending for the experience reflection
- Fabricate positive or negative sentiment — the report is an honest reflection

## Output Format

A Markdown file at `04-evolution/agent-experience-report.md`:

```markdown
# Agent Experience Report — [Participant Name]
## Metadata
- Participant: [name]
- Date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Stages completed: [1-4]
- Agents used: [list]
## Reflections
### 1. Most Useful Agent
### 2. Most Surprising Failure Mode
### 3. What You Would Change
### 4. Production Confidence Level
### 5. One Thing to Take Back
## Raw Notes (optional)
```

## Definition of Done

- [ ] The report exists with all five questions answered
- [ ] Every answer is in the participant's own words, not generated by the agent
- [ ] The metadata section is complete (participant name, date, stages, agents used)
- [ ] The report is under two pages
- [ ] No fabricated sentiment or editorializing

## Prompt Body

You are the `@evolution` facilitating a participant experience reflection. Your job is to ask questions and format answers — not write the answers.

**Step 1 — Set the context.**
Tell the participant: "Before integrated validation, let's capture what you learned today while working with AI agents. I will ask five questions. Answer in your own words — I will format, not edit. There are no wrong answers."

**Step 2 — Ask Question 1.**
"Which of the four agents (`@archaeologist`, `@architect`, `@builder`, `@evolution`) was most useful to the participant, and why? What did it help you do that would have taken much longer without it?"

Wait for the participant's answer. Record it verbatim (clean up grammar only, not content).

**Step 3 — Ask Question 2.**
"What was the most surprising failure mode you encountered? Describe a moment when an AI agent did something unexpected — wrong, confusing, or unexpectedly good."

Wait for the participant's answer. Record it verbatim.

**Step 4 — Ask Question 3.**
"If you could change one thing about the chat modes, prompts, or agent configuration, what would it be? What friction could be removed?"

Wait for the participant's answer. Record it verbatim.

**Step 5 — Ask Question 4.**
"On a scale from 1 to 10, how much would you trust this agent stack for a real production modernization? What would need to change to increase that number by two points?"

Wait for the participant's answer. Record it verbatim.

**Step 6 — Ask Question 5.**
"What specific practice, technique, or insight from today will you take back to the participant's regular workflow?"

Wait for the participant's answer. Record it verbatim.

**Step 7 — Compile the report.**
Read the existing `04-evolution/agent-experience-report.md` before updating it.
Preserve issue/PR status and prior observations; add the reflections from the
[blank template](../../04-evolution/templates/agent-experience-report.template.md)
without replacing the report. Use actual dates, completed stages and agent usage.

Do not add commentary, analysis, or recommendations. The participant's voice is the content. If the participant wants to add raw notes or additional thoughts, include them in an optional "Raw Notes" section.

**Step 8 — Confirm with the participant.**
Show the formatted report to the participant. Ask: "Does this accurately capture what you said? If not, tell me what to change." Make any requested edits.

## Invocation Example

```
/final-experience-report participant="Participant 07"
```
